title: The most expensive Lego sets of all time
content:
Rare Lego sets can fetch thousands of dollars in mint condition, but a set doesn't have to be out of print to fetch high prices. In fact, many of the most expensive Lego sets around are still on sale for sky-high prices. For the curious and the collectors, we've dug through the lot to compile this list of the most expensive Lego on the market - ancient and modern.

If you haven't got new-car money to drop on a Lego relic, you might find something of interest in our guides to the best Lego sets for adults. Or, more more record-setters, here are the absolute biggest Lego sets ever.

The most expensive Lego sets are:mark

  • Cloud City
  • Airport Shuttle
  • 2023 Inside Tour Fire Truck
  • 375 Castle
  • Pirate Skull's Eye Schooner
  • Lego Star Wars Republic Dropship
  • Market Street
  • Space Shuttle
  • Factory AGV
  • Cafe Corner
  • Grand Carousel
  • Death Star II
  • 10179 Millennium Falcon
  • Green Grocer
  • Death Star
  • Millennium Falcon
  • Liebherr Crawler Crane LR 13000
  • Titanic
  • Minas Tirith
  • Pokémon Venusaur Charizard and Blastoise
  • Venator Class Republic Attack Cruiser
  • Eiffel Tower
  • Razor Crest
  • Rivendell
  • Star Trek USS Enterprise
  • Hogsmeade Village
  • Captain Jack Sparrow's Pirate Ship
  • Stranger Things: The Creel House
  • Chocolate Factory
  • FAQ

Lego Cloud City

$12,500

Lego set number 10123
Year released 2003
Number of bricks 698
Current status Retired

There have been many iterations of Lego Cloud City, each recreating the floating mining colony where fans first met Lando Calrissian in The Empire Strikes Back. However, it's the 10123 set that has the most eye-watering price. Its value has reached astronomical heights in recent years - even for a Star Wars set - though the condition of the box has a huge impact on how much it sells for.

Here's a bit of history to show how Cloud City's value has skyrocketed. Second-hand shoppers were paying around $790 (£950) for a like-new copy in 2020. By 2022, this had climbed to $3,270 (£2,700), and in 2023, a set could sell for $9,500 (£7,609). As of 2026, the highest price we've seen came from this eBay sale, which earned an eye-watering $12,500. It's important to note, though, that this is a mint condition copy - less pristine sets have recently sold for closer to $6,000.

Lego Airport Shuttle

$5,307

Lego set number 6399
Year released 1990
Number of bricks 767
Current status Retired

Ah, the 1990s. A time of unbridled American optimism, breakneck technological growth, and massively increased access to air travel! Without breaking out the pink nylon shell suits, it's tough to get more '90s than a Lego set, that's also a trainset, but it's also specifically the cute bright red and yellow monorail shuttle that takes you to the gate for your vacation flight.

No fewer than 27 Town Lego sets came out in 1990, but sealed examples of this one are now worth over five grand, putting it way up in the stakes of most valuable sets of all time. That's maybe partly because of how beautifully it exemplifies the playtime fantasies of its era - but it's also because it's one of the first working, motorized Lego monorail setups, with a ton of flavor, decoration, playability, and customizability.

2023 Inside Tour Lego Fire Truck

$5,000

Lego set number 4000040-1
Year released 2023
Number of bricks 1,056
Current status Retired

Lego's Inside Tours are so exclusive that only 60 tickets are released each year. You have to pay thousands of dollars for a spot, but your reward (along with the tour itself), is one of the most limited-edition Lego sets around. Take, for example, the 2023 Inside Tour Lego Fire Truck. It's designed to look like one of Lego's famous wooden sets from the 1930s, and it celebrates the company's history with a sleek, stylish, and playable model.

Naturally, fans will pay a pretty penny to own this. We've seen second-hand listings climb as high as $7,000, but the highest confirmed sale we've seen belongs to Lego YouTuber DuckBricks. They paid around $5,000 for a box signed by a prestigious Lego designer.

Lego 375 Castle

$4,746

Lego set number 375
Year released 1978
Number of bricks 767
Current status Retired

The 1978 Lego 375 Castle is the most famous variant of the vibrant yellow castles released in the late '70s and early '80s. It was one of the most coveted Lego Castles on release, and it's now one of the most expensive - if it's in mint condition, at least.

The reason for its value? It was the first of the eight 'classic castles' released, and like the Lego Space Command Center, it captures many peoples' childhood memories of Lego. Unfortunately, most of us grew into adults without a spare $5,000 to spend on nostalgia.

Not to worry! If you can bear an unboxed, played-with version with a part or two missing, you could scoop this Lego Castle for less than $360 (£300). A… bargain?

Lego Pirates Skull's Eye Schooner

$4,280

Lego set number 6286
Year released 1993
Number of bricks 912 (though sources differ)
Current status Retired

The Lego Skull's Eye Schooner is a stunning ship and one of the most iconic Pirates kits from the '80s and '90s. Until the mighty Imperial Flagship came along in 2010, the Skull's Eye Schooner was the largest pirate ship that Lego sold, weighing in at 912 pieces. Plus, its prestige means that it remains one of the most expensive pirate Lego sets of all time, even beating out the older Black Seas Barracuda, the original flagship of Captain Redbeard.

There's lots to enjoy about this model, which features movable cannons, three masts, and plenty of lovely minifigures - plus a shark, parrot, and monkey, the most pirate-y animals there are. Collectors enjoy the model very much, which is why a sealed copy of this kit can sell on eBay for just over $4,000.

Lego Star Wars Republic Dropship

$3,599

Ah, Lego Star Wars. You always deliver the goods when it comes to expensive sets. This 2009 set recreates one of the Clone Wars' lesser known but no less essential carriers. The Lego Star Wars Republic Dropship also comes with a ready-to-deploy AT-OT Walker, so that's double the scifi vehicle goodness.

Builders lucky enough to own a copy of this set report that it's as fun to build and play with is it is to display. Sure, Lego designs have become more elegant since the 2000s, but what this set lacks in creativity is makes up for in scarcity. Beware though: as always, only the best-condition sets go for the sort of price we've listed above.

Lego Creator Market Street

$3,393

Lego set number 10190
Year released 2007
Number of bricks 1,248
Current status Retired

Lego Creator's modular buildings are famed for their beauty and relative rarity, and while Lego Creator Market Street has been outclassed aesthetically by modern sets, it remains a firm favorite among collectors. This simple, elegant market was originally designed by early Lego Ambassador Eric Brok who, sadly, died in 2007 and never got to see his creation hit shelves.

As a design from outside of Lego's inner circle, this is one of the more unique Lego Creator sets. The best recent sale we've seen came in September 2025, when an eBay user paid just over $3,000 for a sealed, new copy. As with most Lego sets, that value does diminish drastically if the set is opened and built.

Lego Space Shuttle

$3,051

Lego set number 1593
Year released 1983
Number of bricks 313
Current status Retired

The 1983 Lego Space Shuttle was a small promotional set released in Europe, and in many countries it was sold with packs of Persil laundry powder. That means this isn't one of Lego's most iconic or influential sets - but it's darn hard to get hold of a copy in good condition.

Those rare sealed sets are a tiny treasure trove of nostalgia. The two minifigs that accompany the set mirror those seen in the beloved classic 'Space' line. Even if you weren't around in the days of vintage Lego, you'll recognize this smiling yellow face from 2014's Lego movie. Ask anyone to imagine a LEGO minifigure, and a good number of them will conjure up a vision of an astronaut; the star of LEGO Space.

The top-end of this set's value is around $3,000, as demonstrated by this eBay sale from November 2025.

Lego Factory AGV

$2,999

Lego set number 4000037-1
Year released 2022
Number of bricks 803
Current status Retired

Automated Guided Vehicles are real-life machines used to transport Lego bricks across the factory floor. 2022's Lego Inside Tour celebrated this crucial part of the company's logistics with a unique set, exclusive to the select few that attended that year's tour.

The Lego Factory AGV is small and simple, but its concept (and, by the looks of it, color) is utterly unique. No wonder, then, that a box signed by the designers sold on eBay in October 2025 for just shy of $3,000.

Lego Cafe Corner

$2,719

Lego set number 10182
Year released 2007
Number of bricks 2,044
Current status Retired

Lego Cafe Corner is the very first of the iconic modular buildings series. The collect-o-mania that this series inspired hadn't quite kicked off until this set was retired, so mint condition copies are extremely desirable. This set is so influential and so iconic that even individual parts can sell for a pretty penny.

While the condition of a set always matters, owners of mint condition copies can expect at least a few thousand dollars. Recently, we saw one set sell on eBay for just shy of three thousand.

Lego Grand Carousel

$2,503

Lego set number 10196
Year released 2009
Number of bricks 3,263
Current status Retired

The Lego Grand Carousel is a rare, one-of-a-kind display piece, a functional carousel that even plays music as its tiny horses spin. It's a set that really shows off the intricacy and beauty that Lego Creator sets can achieve. It's a painfully repetitive build, yes, but if you're purely looking to collect a rare and valuable set, that probably won't bother you.

New, sealed sets can go for as high as $2,500, as seen in an eBay sale from November 2025. This might not be the most famous set of the early 2000s, but sealed copies still vastly outpace the original RRP of $250.

Lego Death Star II

$2,499

Lego set number 10143
Year released 2005
Number of bricks 3,447
Current status Retired

There have been many Lego Death Stars, but when fans gather to debate which was best, there are usually two schools of thought. The first prefers the playability of the 75159, but lovers of history and display pieces gravitate towards the Lego 10143 Death Star II. This depicts the second Death Star we see in the movies, still under construction as it floats through space.

It's a hefty build, with not much variation and zero play value. However, it's probably the most epic the Death Star has ever looked in Lego form. Its age and scarcity add further value, with sealed sets selling for as much as $2,499 on eBay as of November 2025.

Lego 10179 Millennium Falcon

$2,492

Lego set number 10179
Year released 2007
Number of bricks 5,197
Current status Retired

The Lego 10179 Millennium Falcon isn't considered the best depiction of Han Solo's iconic ship. That accolade now goes to a later UCS set with more bricks and better detailing. However, this version of the Falcon is still celebrated as the first, charming for its time, even if younger models have outclassed it.

Plus, its age means it's definitely the scarcer of the Falcons. That alone is enough to push a set's price up. The best we've seen lately was an eBay sale in October 2025, where the ship netted just short of 2.5k.

Lego Creator Expert: Green Grocer

$1,913

Lego set number 10185
Year released 2008
Number of bricks 2,352
Current status Retired

The Lego Creator Expert: Green Grocer set was the third in the Modular Building series, which gave advanced builders a realistic grocery store to put together.

Unlike the previous two Modular Buildings, the Green Grocer came with a highly detailed interior. While the outside had railings, opening windows, a fire escape, and a courtyard, the inside boasted a fully-furnished first floor, complete with food to sell to minifig customers.

As an early entry in a popular series, the Green Grocer is naturally coveted. It's also a beautiful, complex build that was discontinued in 2010. Scarcity, quality, and history all make this an extremely valuable find.

Nowadays, you can pick one up for anywhere between $800 and $2,000, depending on condition. Our current price estimate is based on a sale made on eBay in November 2025.

Lego Death Star

$999.99

Lego set number 75419
Year released 2025
Number of bricks 9,023
Current status Available

The Lego Death Star one of the newest additions to this list - released on October 4, 2025, it's blasted Rivendell out of the top 20, leaving a smoldering pile of bricks like the ruins of Alderaan. It may well creep a few places higher in time, since the kits above it are boosted by the fact they're out of production, and this is launching at an eye-watering price - just one cent short of a round thousand dollars.

There was a little controversy when the Lego Death Star was announced, since - like many licensed Star Wars kits - you're partly paying for the licensing fees, and the price per brick is high. The Lego Titanic and Lego Eiffel Tower are each more than $300 cheaper, and contain more pieces.

Rather than a stud-covered grey football, the cutaway design is packed with interior details, drawn from both versions of the Death Star (and incongruously, Darth Vader's meditation chamber from the Executor). The back of the kit is not appealing - it's designed to be pushed up against a wall. But it does come with an edifying 38 minifigures, more than enough to re-enact all your favorite scenes from the original trilogy (we're picturing something like Dark Helmet from Space Balls).

Lego Millennium Falcon

$849.99

Lego set number 75192
Year released 2017
Number of bricks 7,500
Current status Available

There are few pieces of Star Wars memorabilia more iconic than the legendary 75192 UCS Lego Millennium Falcon, which Lego calls "the largest, most detailed Lego Star Wars Millennium Falcon model we've ever created". As a result, it's permanently among the top-priced sets you can buy.

When it is available from the Lego Store, it'll cost you $850 (£735) - already up there with the most expensive production sets - but even then it's generally listed as "hard to find". And when stocks run out, scarcity drives the used prices up to well above $1,000. We've regularly seen the boxed set sold on eBay for anywhere between $500 and $1,750. Heck, we've seen people try to sell the instructions alone for $60.

Lego Liebherr Crawler Crane LR 13000

$699.99

Lego set number 42146
Year released 2023
Number of pieces 2,883
Current status Available

The first of our expensive Lego sets that can still be bought from the official store, Lego's latest 'engineer's dream' option, the gigantic Liebherr Crawler Crane is a three-foot-tall, fully motorized, app-controlled construction vehicle par excellence. It's well in the running to be named the best Lego Technic set ever released.

Billed as a "tribute to one of the world's most powerful cranes", this behemoth is a complex build project aimed at adults - not one for the kids' Christmas presents. But the result is a completely realistic, electronic working model, able to drive around freely on its caterpillar tracks, accurately extend its articulated crane arm, and pick things up - all via remote control from the included smartphone app.

Lego Titanic

$679.99

Lego set number 10294
Year released 2021
Number of pieces 9,090
Current status Available

With over 9,000 pieces, the majestic Lego Titanic is a truly herculean build challenge worthy of the famous ship's name.

Both externally and internally, the Titanic set has been designed as an authentic replica of the real ocean liner that went down in 1912, down to every deck, staircase, and porthole. The ship detaches into three vertically sliced cross sections, letting you see below-deck areas, including the famous grand staircase shown off so memorably in James Cameron's movie.

And, in a glorious touch of interactivity, the piston engines in the engine room are mechanically linked to the propeller at the back - so spin the prop, and the engine starts going. This set is vast, incredibly heavy, and eye-wateringly expensive, but, for ship-loving history buffs, it's all but essential.

Lord of the Rings - Minas Tirith

$649.99

Lego set number 11377
Year released 2026
Number of pieces 8,278
Current status Coming soon (June 4, 2026)

The newest and most expensive of LEGO's heart-achingly magnificent Lord of the Rings mega-sets, Minas Tirith has lit a LOT of folks' beacons (including ours) since it was revealed in May 2026. At 8,278 pieces, it's up there in the size stakes - bigger than its Middle-earth siblings Rivendell and Barad-Dur. That beefy scale costs money, of course: at 650 bucks, this immediately becomes the joint fifth most expensive Lego set currently in production.

But, like those others before it, Minas Tirith's premium price also buys you a frankly bewildering wealth of movie details. It's got the 'detachable playset' element from Rivendell - in this case the whole outer curtain wall becomes a courtyard.

But it's also cribbed notes from Barad-Dur, with a mighty cross section interior, complete with Gondor's towering, empty throne room, the candlelit library where Gandalf researched the Rings of Power, and even the little "so do all who live to see such times" balcony. You get 10 Return of the King-flavored minifigures, too - and even a Lego Palantir!

Pokémon Venusaur, Charizard and Blastoise

$649.99

Lego set number 72153
Year released 2026
Number of pieces 6,838
Current status Coming soon

Considering that the Venn diagram of 'people who buy expensive Lego sets' and 'people emotionally invested in the original 1990s starter Pokémon' is very nearly a circle, it's surprising we haven't had any Pokémon Lego sets before now.  Anyway, better late than never, and Lego is going hard for its very first round of official Pokésets in 2026, celebrating Pokémon's 30th anniversary year.

The flagship set, Venusaur, Charizard and Blastoise, is an undeniable stunner, rendering the fully evolved forms of Gen 1's beloved starters in surprising detail with a whopping 6,838 bricks, in all the bright primary colors your inner child could possibly desire. Their gorgeous circular diorama base, placing Venusaur amid jungle plants, Blastoise on top of a Surf wave, and Charizard literally flying above a pillar of lava rock, takes this from 'very good set' to 'landmark collectible', in our view.

The biggest downside is what buys it a place in this list: a Paralyze-inducing price tag of 650 bucks. We're not exactly surprised; a huge new premium model, plus the Pokémon factor, is going to end up with a very expensive Lego set. But if you're just looking for a massive, once in a lifetime build worth remembering the Titanic set above offers over 2,000 more pieces for only 30 dollars more.

Lego Venator Class Republic Attack Cruiser

$649.99

Lego set number 75367
Year released 2023
Number of pieces 5,374
Current status Available

Star Wars fans went wild for the Lego Venator-Class Republic Attack Cruiser when it was released, and with good reason: it's a gigantic, super detailed recreation of a fan-favorite (or perhaps cult classic) Star Wars ship.

The Millennium Falcon, Star Destroyer, and AT-AT may be household names, but the Venator - a warship that was a prequel-era precursor to the Star Destroyer - is better known to fans of the Clone Wars animated series. The UCS Lego set version pays tribute to that with a design carefully tuned to the ship seen in the show (and fleetingly in Episodes II and III). All the surface details are on point, down to the tiny Republic Gunship in the side hangar.

The Venator only includes two minifigures, and it has very little interactivity compared to other big-money mega-sets. However, hardcore Clone Wars lovers might forgive the static display piece for these few faults.

Lego Eiffel Tower

$629.99

Lego set number 10307
Year released 2022
Number of pieces 10,001
Current status Available

For us, the Lego Eiffel Tower is the king of architectural Lego sets. At over 10,000 pieces, it's the tallest Lego set, and has the second highest piece count of any set. While its $630 (£555) price tag makes it among the most expensive sets, it's arguably one of the best-value giant sets, simply for the colossal amount of Lego you're getting for the price, compared to similarly priced sets above that have around half the pieces.

It's not all about piece count, though; the Eiffel Tower set is a famously challenging, four-stage building project designed to mirror how the real Parisian tower was built - and buyers should beware that a huge proportion of those 10,000 bricks are near-identical grey struts. This is a high-price set, and what you're paying for is a mechanically satisfying marathon build, to get a huge, classy display piece - not a breezy family fun-time.

Lego Razor Crest

$599.99

Lego set number 75331
Year released 2022
Number of pieces 6,187
Current status Retiring soon

When The Mandalorian hit Disney+ in 2019, it introduced fans to three unforgettable characters: The Child (Grogu); Mando himself; and his ship, the Razor Crest. Three years and another TV season later, the Lego Razor Crest was added to the Ultimate Collector series to commemorate Mando's modified ST-70 Assault Ship.

This 6,187-piece beast is loaded with details from the show, including an interior fully modeled with blaster racks, escape pod, and carbon freezing chamber - but the main draw is the scale and fidelity of the overall build. It'll take you 18 hours to build, but the resulting model, like all the UCS sets, is an impressive display piece.

Also like its fellow UCS sets, the Razor Crest will cost you nearly half a month's rent, retailing at 600 bucks. This set is due to retire soon, though, which will push prices much higher - so if this one is a must for your collection, we'd recommend picking it up wherever you can find stock now.

Lego Rivendell

$499.99

Lego set number 10316
Year released 2023
Number of pieces 6,167
Current status Available

At $500 (£429), the Lego Rivendell set is among the top ten most expensive Lego sets currently on store shelves - but it's also stunningly true to the Rivendell we see in The Fellowship of the Ring. We get detailed sections for Bilbo's writing room, Arwen's ornate white gazebo, the reliquary where the shards of Narsil were kept, and - of course - the courtyard that plays host to the fateful Council of Elrond.

A whopping 15 minifigures, including the entire Fellowship, are the icing on an already mouth-watering cake. Rivendell may be an expensive Lego set, but it's been on our Christmas list for a long time now.

Lego Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise

$399.99

Lego set number 10356
Year released 2025
Number of pieces 3,600
Current status Available

Federation scientists are still working on the fiendish puzzle of just how it took Lego just shy of 40 years to create a set based on the best version of the starship Enterprise, from the best version of Star Trek (no, we will not be taking questions at this time).

But, at long last, here it is: the Lego Star Trek Enterprise-D, all 3,600 pieces and nine minifigures of it, released on Black Friday, November 28, 2025. We can see why it's got trekkies so excited; there's even a detachable saucer section for when the alien soil samples really hit the fan!

Yes, most of the bricks are light grey (just as they should be) so if that turns you off for Star Wars Star Destroyers, it will here too. But for die hard TNG enjoyers, the chance to build this inimitably wonderful craft and display it on your shelf forever is surely unmissable. If that's not enough, the Lieutenant Worf minifigure's headpiece integrates his Klingon brow ridges, and there's a Wesley minifig you can shout "Shut up Wesley!" at! Sold.

Lego Hogsmeade Village

$399.99

Lego set number 76457
Year released 2025
Number of pieces 3,228
Current status Available

Remember the 2021 set 'Hogsmeade Village Visit'? This is what she looks like now. Aside from the setting, there's very little in common between the kid-friendly set 76388 and the behemoth Lego Hogsmeade Village set 76457.  This is a full Christmas village display in Lego form, a complete row of Lego houses, and another massive Harry Potter set. Definitely one for the adult Potterheads.

Captain Jack Sparrow's Pirate Ship

$379.99

Lego set number 10365
Release date 2025
Number of pieces 2,862
Current status Available

The ship's called the Black Pearl, by the way, Lego, but 22 years on from the original movie it's probably a good call to name this after Johnny Depp's iconic drunken pirate. Were it not for the Johnny Depp, Orlando Bloom, and Kiera Knightley minifigures, Lego Jack Sparrow's Pirate Ship could practically be a kit from Lego's classic Pirates range. But at about one twentieth the price and three times the size of an original Skull's Eye Schooner, it's probably the right choice if you want a massive Lego Pirate ship.

Lego Stranger Things: The Creel House

$299.99

Lego set number 11370
Release date 2026
Number of pieces 2,593
Current status Available

OK, so the final season of Stranger Things has left many fans with mixed feelings thanks to a few plot holes and that weirdly long, soppily self indulgent 30 minute epilogue. But there's no doubting that Season 4's GNARLY haunted house, childhood home of uber-antagonist Vecna a.k.a. Henry Creel, was both scary and awesome.

The Lego Creel House is brand new in January 2026, and on the surface it looks like the real Hawkins version we saw in season four: tumbledown and boarded up. But the set overall is packed with season five details, from Steve's ill fated red BMW and the WSQK 'The Squawk' radio truck, to a rotating deck with tweed-suited friendly Mr Whatsit on one side and veiny, evil Vecna on the other. Also, you get a whopping 13 minifigures including all the core gang, plus Holly (yay), minus Hopper (boo).

Lego Chocolate Factory

$219.99

Lego set number 21360
Release date 2025
Number of pieces 2,025
Current status Available

Yet another big screen adaptation, this set is inspired by the timeless 1971 Gene Wilder movie based on Roald Dahl's classic children's book. Though the bright colors might appeal to kids, the price tag - and the fact that this is referencing a movie from over half a century ago - mean the Lego Chocolate Factory is definitely going to be a collector's item. Sadly, none of this appears to be edible, meaning our dreams of drinking from a chocolate river must still go unfulfilled.

Most expensive Lego sets FAQ

If you're not a seasoned brickhead, the world of high-value, rare Lego sets can be a rather strange place - below we'll answer a few of the most common queries from folks new to Lego collecting.

Why are retired Lego sets so expensive?

When a Lego set is officially 'Retired', it means it's reached the end of its production cycle, and Lego will not make any more of it. Ordinarily, the Lego Store will actually mark a set 'Retiring Soon' when it has stopped producing more of that set, meaning that its remaining stock will be the last.

By the simple law of supply and demand, this means that when a set gets marked for retirement, its price will tend to start going up because of the set's increasing scarcity; if something's harder to get, but people still want it, sellers can charge them more.

Does Lego ever 'un-retire' sets?

No - typically, once a Lego set has been retired, Lego never puts it back into full production. However, some more popular sets do get remade into completely new sets - this has happened with the Lego Taj Mahal and several popular Star Wars sets.

One exception was the Lego Legends range, first released in 2001, which re-published seven highly popular sets, with refreshed packaging and new set numbers. It seems this experiment didn't work out, though, because Lego has never repeated it since.

What was the first Lego set ever?

It depends on what you're counting as a Lego set - but if we're just talking about something we'd recognize as a set today - a dedicated model using the 'Lego System' of studded plastic bricks - then the first one ever is Garage with Automatic Door (set number 2026) released in 1956. YouTuber LetsBuild has a great video on it:

What's the best place to buy classic, retired Lego sets?

If you're after older retired Lego sets in boxed, like new condition, the first port of call is probably eBay - but you can expect to pay a lot (just look at some of the set prices above to get an idea!)

However, a more popular way to get your hands on older sets is to use the frankly miraculous used Lego web store Bricklink, which not only provides a marketplace to buy used sets, but also contains complete lists of the individual pieces you need to reconstruct the set yourself! You'll have to buy the instructions too, but they usually only cost a few pennies.

And that's it for our roundup of the most expensive Lego sets of all time - for now! For more lists of great sets, here are the best Star Wars Lego sets.

title: DnD release schedule 2026 and 2027
content:
The DnD release schedule for 2026 has almost wrapped up, with just one season of launches left. We've seen horrors, and we've seen arcane marvels. Now, though, our eyes our looking forward to the upcoming DnD books of 2027. You can learn all about Dungeons and Dragons' latest books below, with handy summaries of what's just come out - and what's next.

If you're after more evergreen info, check out our guides to DnD classes and DnD races. These offer every bit of info you might need to start building your next character. For now, though, let's talk releases.

Here's the current DnD release schedule:

  • World of Warcraft
  • Dark Sun
  • Greyhawk: Crown of the Witch Queen
  • Star Wars
  • Untitled Greyhawk book
  • D&D Beyond Partnered Content
  • Most recent D&D books
  • Arcana Unleashed

D&D: World of Warcraft

Release date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026

Our mystery winter product is, in fact, the start of D&D's new Universes Beyond line. D&D: World of Warcraft takes us to the famed world of Azeroth. We're getting a treasure trove of rules here, with 13 WoW-specific classes, nine subclasses, and 40 specializations.

Wizards has also promised 16 new species, 60+ spells, and 25+ magic items. This might be one of the most ambitious D&D books of the year, but will the crossover be any good? Only time will tell.

Dark Sun

Release date: 2027

It's the one reboot we never thought they'd do! D&D returns to Dark Sun in early 2027, and it's not shying away from the apocalyptic's settings grit and gore. The two sourcebooks, Edge of Oblivion and Blood & Power, are D&D's first R-rated books, with so much edgy art that they'll come shrink-wrapped. They'll also come with an all-new Psion class, a guide to the setting, and a bunch of new character options.

Greyhawk: Crown of the Witch Queen

Release date: 2027

We return to D&D's oldest setting in Greyhawk: Crown of the Witch Queen. The big bad of this new campaign is Drelzna, the vampire daughter of Igwilv. You may also know Igwilv as Tasha, archfey, witch queen, and all around badass. We don't expect her daughter will go down easy…

D&D Star Wars

Release date: 2027

When Darth Vader walked across the stage of D&D's Gen Con keynote, one thing became clear: D&D Star Wars is making an official comeback. We don't know much about what the Season of Rebellion looks like yet. We do know, though, that it'll continue Wizards' new Universes Beyond strategy trialed with World of Warcraft. May the Force be with anyone who gives this unusual crossover a go.

Untitled Greyhawk book

Release date: 2027?

Wizards of the Coast has confirmed that one more official D&D book is in the works. We just don't know what it's called or when it's coming out.

What we do know is it's being developed by Luke Gygax, son of D&D's original creator. Luke's original character, Melf the Elf, is now a key part of D&D canon, and it looks like he'll be our starring guide for this Greyhawk tour. Art has been shared of Melf on the cover of this as-yet-untitled book, but that's as much detail as we're getting right now.

D&D Beyond Partnered Content

We're only getting a handful of official D&D books this year, but D&DBeyond remains a busy marketplace. That's thanks to the horde of partnered content coming to the platform. Here's a rundown of all the new, third-party books, and when they become available:

  • Exploring Eberron - January 27
  • The Pugilist Class - February 3
  • Faster, Purple Worm! Everybody Dies, Vol 1 - February 24
  • Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting: Part 2 - Early March
  • The Griffon's Saddlebag: Book One - Late March
  • Dr Dhrolin's Dictionary of Dinosaurs - April
  • Tom Cartos Sticker Packs - April
  • Northlands Worldbook - May
  • Northlands Sagas - May
  • Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt Player Pack - June
  • Valda's Spire of Secrets: Player Pack 2 - July
  • Vampire: The Masquerade - Bound by Blood - July
  • Legends of Greyhawk: Saviors of Safeton - July
  • Frontiers of Eberron: Quickstone - August
  • The Field Guide to Floral Dragons - August
  • Legends of Greyhawk: Dreams of the Chained God - August
  • Legends of Greyhawk: The Tear-Stained Idol - September
  • The Magus Class - September 29
  • Legends of Greyhawk: Heralds of the Old One - October
  • Obojima: Tales from Yatamon - October 27
  • Legends of Greyhawk: The Ruins of Castle Greyhawk - November
  • Legends of Greyhawk: Beasts of Johrase - December
  • Warlord Player Pack - December 1
  • Herbarium - December 15

Most recent DnD books

Arcana Unleashed

Release date: Tuesday, September 15, 2026

Releasing in September, Arcana Unleashed is all about new magic options. That means a heap more subclasses, spells, magical feats, and unique items for your party inventory. It also means new guidance on working for magical patrons and factions, plus a little bit of adventure content to boot.

Personally, I'd call this the best 5.5e book so far. The ideas are original and exciting. The new character options are generally strong, with a few really interesting standouts. Not every concept Wizards introduces flies flawlessly, but there's far more good than bad.

Read our full 9/10 Arcana Unleashed review here.

Arcana Unleashed Deadfall

Release date: Tuesday, September 15, 2026

Arcana Unleashed Deadfall is a companion adventure for the previous book on the release schedule. Starting at level 11, this high-stakes espionage campaign takes you all the way to level 20. The goal? Infiltrate the Red Wizards of Thay in order to stop the necromantic machinations of one Szass Tam.

It's a solid concept, but Wizards sadly doesn't deliver. The narrative is shallow, the gameplay gets repetitive, and the high challenge level will either delight your masochistic party or drive them away altogether.

Learn more in my Arcana Unleashed: Deadfall review.

Ravenloft: The Horrors Within

Release date: Tuesday, June 16, 2026

First off the blocks is Ravenloft: The Horrors Within - a "Gameplay Expansion" (a.k.a. rulebook) that returns us to the Domains of Dread, featuring everyone's favorite romantically challenged immortal maniac, Count Strahd von Zarovich. Oh, and also Cthulhu is here!

Several horror-themed subclasses appear alongside revised 'lineage' species options and a heap of tempting yet terrifying Dark Power feats. Many of these feel familiar to longtime 5e players, but the remastered rules feel significantly more streamlined. Plus, the all-new Hollow Warden Ranger is seriously exciting.

Beyond player-facing options, we get stat blocks for a heap of Darklords, plus a whistlestop tour of the most famous dread demiplanes - including the Lovecraftian Innsmouth. There's some great campaign fodder here, though the stripped-back lore feels less rich than when we last saw it in Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft.

Find out why we gave the book a 7/10 in our full Ravenloft: The Horrors Within review.

That's all for now! Though, if you'd like to keep talking about Dungeons and Dragons, join us for a chat in the Wargamer Discord.

Yugioh banlist FAQ

What is the Yu Gi Oh banlist?

Yugioh TCG publisher Konami releases an updated version of the Yu Gi Oh banlist every few months. This lists all the restrictions on the cards you can include in constructed Yu Gi Oh! decks (and tells you when previously banned or restricted cards have been unbanned!)

The three restricted types in Yugioh banlist are:

  • Forbidden - This card cannot be used in your Main Deck, Extra Deck, or Side Deck.
  • Limited / Limited 1 - You can only have one copy of this card in your main Deck, Extra Deck, and Side Deck combined.
  • Semi-limited / Limited 2 - You can only have two copies of this card in your Main Deck, Extra Deck, and Side Deck combined.

There are separate banlists for the game's 'Advanced' format (which is used in Regional, National, and World Championship events) and the much looser 'Traditional' format. For example, many cards are Forbidden in Advanced, but only Limited in Traditional format.

Forbidden, Limited, and Semi-limited cards can be cards of any type, and the Yu Gi Oh banlist typically contains numerous Monster, Monster/Effect, Monster/Fusion, Monster/Link, Monster/Synchro, Monster/Xyz, Spell, and Trap type cards.

Why do Yugioh cards get banned?

As with all the best trading card games, the Yugioh TCG regularly releases new sets of cards to keep the game fresh and offer players new strategies, themes, and options for their decks. When players get their hands on the new cards,  they quickly discover the most powerful options, especially cards that create strong combo effects with existing or older cards. This is, of course, part of the fun!

However, it can lead to just a handful of decks becoming dominant, able to beat any other decks they face - and thus the game's overall scene (often called its 'meta') becomes very samey, as everyone is forced to play with similar decks and cards if they want to have a chance of winning games.

Konami generally tries to maintain competitive balance with the range of new cards it releases - but with a game as complex and high-powered as Yugioh, cards will always emerge that 'warp the meta' and generate bad player feedback.

These are the sorts of cards that end up getting banned - either Semi-Limited, Limited or Forbidden - because they:

  • Are inherently too powerful (normally in combat power).
  • Are part of a combo that is too powerful / too easy to win with.
  • Are too versatile in cancelling out, or 'shutting down' multiple other strategies.
  • Are likely to cause problems in one of the above ways, after an upcoming release joins the meta.

Are there any permanently banned Yugioh cards?

While there's no official status for a Yugioh card being banned forever, there are a few cards we expect will never return from the Forbidden zone, because the features that made them too powerful are only becoming more overpowered as time goes on.

Because matches of the Yugioh TCG can be dominated by extremely powerful, quick combo plays that can end the game very quickly, some of the most powerful banned cards tend to be ones that let you draw extra cards, or find exactly the cards you need from your deck, without a significant cost attached.

The three most prominent examples of these long banned cards are:

  • Pot of Greed (Spell card) Draw two cards.
  • Painful Choice (Spell card) Select five cards from your deck and show them to your opponent. They choose one card to add to your hand, and the rest go to your Graveyard.
  • Graceful Charity (Spell card) Draw three cards, then discard two cards.

What's the difference between the Yugioh TCG and OCG?

There are two separate forms of the Yu-Gi-Oh! card game: the Trading Card Game (TCG) - which is sold and played worldwide, with cards printed in English and several European languages - and the Official Card Game (OCG), which is only available in Japanese language, and played mainly in Japan.

The Japanese OCG has a different release schedule for new sets and products; it runs on slightly different tournament rules; it gets its own exclusive cards not available in the TCG; and it has its own separate banlist of Forbidden and Limited cards, which gets updated via its own Japanese language website.

It's a key difference from the Pokémon TCG, where the main differences between Japanese Pokémon cards and English ones are in the card designs, print quality, and release schedule, but the game rules are the same and there's no structural separation between the two.

And that's it for our complete guide to the official Yugioh TCG banlist - for now! If you want to trade hot takes and predictions for upcoming bans, or just hype about Yugioh and every other bangin' tabletop game on the planet, join us in the free Wargamer Discord community!
